Answer: Entailment
Confidence: 80%

Section 2(a)(2)(B) is the limitation rule stating that a taxpayer shall not be considered a surviving spouse unless a joint return could have been made in the year the spouse died. Since Alice was a nonresident alien during all of 2014, the statute explicitly states "no joint return shall be made" - meaning this limitation is triggered and "applies" to Bob. The main risk is interpreting "applies" as meaning Bob satisfies it (would make him a surviving spouse) rather than that the limitation rule is simply triggered by his circumstances.
reasoning:
Let me reconsider this carefully.

Section 2(a)(2)(B) states:
"Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for purposes of section 1 a taxpayer shall not be considered to be a surviving spouse-
(A) if the taxpayer has remarried at any time before the close of the taxable year, or
(B) unless, for the taxpayer's taxable year during which his spouse died, a joint return could have been made. A husband and wife may make a single return jointly of income taxes, even though one of the spouses has neither gross income nor deductions, except that no joint return shall be made if either the husband or wife at any time during the taxable year is a nonresident alien."

So Section 2(a)(2)(B) is a limitation that says: a taxpayer shall NOT be considered a surviving spouse UNLESS a joint return could have been made.

The facts show Alice was a nonresident alien during 2014 (she became one in 1990). Section 2(a)(2)(B) says "no joint return shall be made if either the husband or wife at any time during the taxable year is a nonresident alien."

So the key question is: "Does Section 2(a)(2)(B) apply to Bob in 2014?"

The phrase "Section 2(a)(2)(B) applies" could mean:
1. The provision IS triggered/relevant to Bob's situation
2. The provision IS satisfied/makes Bob eligible as a surviving spouse

Reading the question as a legal entailment task: If the claim is "Section 2(a)(2)(B) applies to Bob in 2014" and we're checking if this is true given the statute and facts.

Section 2(a)(2)(B) is a rule that DISQUALIFIES someone from being a surviving spouse if a joint return could not have been made. Since Alice was a nonresident alien, no joint return could be made. So the limitation in 2(a)(2)(B) IS triggered/applies.


The answer is Entailment.
